headline: ALBOR EXPANDS: MOGOTES DRILLS 180M AT 0.98% CUEQ — COPPER-GOLD-MOLY NEXT TO BHP-LUNDIN'S FILO DEL SOL (TSXV:MOG)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Mogotes Metals Inc.
snippet: Mogotes Metals (TSXV: MOG) reported July 9 that drilling at the Albor target within its Filo Sur project in Argentina's Vicuña District has returned 180 metres at 0.98% copper equivalent — including an 86-metre interval at 0.70% Cu, 0.55 g/t Au, 2.7 g/t Ag, and 169 ppm Mo, with a 43-metre higher-grade core at 1.1% Cu and 0.82 g/t Au. Filo Sur sits immediately south of and along strike from the Filo del Sol copper-gold-silver project being advanced by BHP and Lundin Mining, making Albor the second porphyry-scale copper-gold-molybdenum discovery by Mogotes in its first drilling season and one of the most strategically positioned junior copper finds in a district that already hosts a globally significant resource under active development by two of the world's largest miners.

headline: GOGOLD PARRAL HITS 5-YEAR SILVER HIGH: 477,464 AGEQ OZ IN JUNE QUARTER, CASH GROWS TO $284M (TSX:GGD)
source_name: Globe and Mail / GoGold Resources Inc.
snippet: GoGold Resources (TSX: GGD) announced July 9 that the Parral tailings operation in Chihuahua, Mexico delivered 477,464 silver equivalent ounces in the June 2026 quarter — a 21% increase over the prior quarter and the highest quarterly silver production in five years — with 268,673 silver ounces, 3,036 gold ounces, 88 tonnes of copper, and 116 tonnes of zinc produced. The company's cash position grew by approximately US$22 million to US$284 million with zero debt, placing GoGold in an exceptional financial position to advance its Los Ricos development project in Jalisco; at $58/oz silver, a five-year production high from a debt-free tailings operation generating US$22M+ in quarterly cash surplus is one of the stronger silver company operating stories in the junior-to-mid-tier space right now.

headline: G MINING VENTURES Q2 GOLD OUTPUT +16% TO 36,845 OZ — TOCANTINZINHO ON PACE, H2 GRADE UPLIFT STILL TO COME (TSX:GMIN)
snippet: G Mining Ventures (TSX: GMIN) reported July 9 preliminary Q2 2026 gold production of 36,845 ounces from its 100%-owned Tocantinzinho mine in Pará, Brazil — up 16% from Q1's 31,846 ounces — with YTD output of 68,691 ounces on track for full-year guidance of 160,000–190,000 ounces, with 62% of output weighted to H2. Record Q2 waste stripping of 6.3 million tonnes at 91.9% average gold recovery is advancing access to Phase 2 higher-grade mineralisation, so the grade improvement that management projected for H2 has not yet started; investors in Tocantinzinho are still ahead of the improving cash-flow trajectory that the project's original economics were built on, now operating at gold prices well above those PEA assumptions.

headline: MADSEN MINE: 53.87 G/T AU OVER 3.1M AND 43.38 G/T AU OVER 3.85M IN VIRGIN AUSTIN COMPLEXES (TSXV:WRLG)
source_name: GlobeNewswire / West Red Lake Gold Mines Ltd.
snippet: West Red Lake Gold Mines (TSXV: WRLG) released July 7 assay results from the Austin 955 and 904 Complexes at the Madsen Mine in Northwestern Ontario — the 955 Complex returning 43.38 g/t Au over 3.85m and 53.87 g/t Au over 3.1m from the 12 Level at approximately 600 metres depth, and the 904 Complex delivering 10.22 g/t Au over 13.35m from the 13 Level at approximately 650 metres. The Austin 904 comprises an approximately 200m-by-200m panel of intact, non-remnant gold mineralisation not historically mined — a rare find inside a 1970s-vintage mine — and management is targeting its sequencing into the H1 2027 mine plan, which would convert a drill-defined block into near-term production cash flow at current gold prices above $4,000.

headline: GENESIS TABLES A$5.6B RIVAL BID FOR VAULT — CREATES A$12.6B AUSTRALIAN GOLD GIANT, REGIS MUST RESPOND BY JULY 10
source_name: Motley Fool Australia / Genesis Minerals Ltd.
snippet: Genesis Minerals has tabled a binding A$5.6 billion cash-and-stock proposal to merge with Vault Minerals — implying A$5.2741 per share, a 14.5% premium to Vault's existing all-stock deal with Regis Resources — with Vault's board unanimously declaring Genesis's offer superior and triggering a five-business-day matching period for Regis that expires July 10. A combined Genesis-Vault entity would be a A$12.6 billion Australian gold producer targeting 600,000–700,000 oz annually, with an estimated A$2 billion in post-tax synergies driven by overlapping operations within 35 kilometres of each other in Western Australia's Leonora-Laverton district — a structural advantage that makes the synergy case genuinely compelling and structurally difficult for Regis to replicate with a counter-offer.

headline: LITHIUMBANK SECURES LOI ON BOARDWALK WELLS AND PIPELINES — EXISTING OILFIELD INFRASTRUCTURE CUTS BRINE CAPEX (TSXV:LBNK)
source_name: Globe and Mail / LithiumBank Resources Corp.
snippet: LithiumBank Resources (TSXV: LBNK) announced July 9 a non-binding LOI to acquire existing wells, pipelines, surface leases, and easements adjacent to its 100%-owned Boardwalk Lithium Brine Project in northwest Alberta — infrastructure the company says will "materially reduce capital expenditures and shorten the timeline" to development, complementing two Leduc Formation producing wells already acquired (10-6 and 1-12). Boardwalk hosts one of North America's largest in-situ lithium brine resources, and the strategy of assembling legacy oilfield infrastructure rather than drilling new wells targets a lower-capex, modular development path currently being assessed in a Feasibility Study — a differentiated financing approach in an environment where high-capex battery metals projects have struggled for capital.

headline: LUNDIN: MINERS LAGGING GOLD BY GENERATIONAL MARGINS — THIS WASHOUT IS THE STRONGEST ENTRY POINT OF THE CYCLE
snippet: Gold Newsletter publisher Brien Lundin argues in a July 2026 GoldSeek piece that gold mining and silver stocks have lagged physical gold by wider margins than at any comparable point in this bull cycle — because central banks provided a non-speculative, price-insensitive foundation under bullion that never triggered the typical Western retail rotation into miners and silver — creating what Lundin calls a "generational opportunity" in which the equity leverage to a move already embedded in gold prices remains unclaimed. He identifies mid-July to mid-August as the seasonal turning point and frames the recent mining equity washout as a positioning flush rather than a fundamental breakdown, with his long-term gold target of $6,000–$8,000 making current miner valuations at depressed gold a compounding mispricing that historically has not persisted beyond 12–18 months.

headline: JAGUAR LAUNCHES 5,000M DIRECTIONAL DRILL BELOW PILAR MINE — BA, LPA AND BF ZONES TARGETED BELOW 1,100M (TSX:JAG)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Jaguar Mining Inc.
snippet: Jaguar Mining (TSX: JAG) commenced a 5,000-metre directional drilling program at the operating Pilar Gold Mine in Minas Gerais, Brazil on July 9 — targeting the BA, LPA, and BF mineralized zones below the current mine's 1,100-metre depth limit, with the program expected to run 10–12 months as part of the company's 227,200-metre five-year exploration campaign. Using directional drilling from existing underground infrastructure, Jaguar is targeting over 500,000 ounces of potential new gold endowment below current production horizons — an approach that eliminates new development heading costs and represents a separate exploration thesis from the company's district-scale Paciência Trend corridor announced earlier this week; a confirmed plunge extension would materially extend Pilar's current eight-year mine life.

headline: SPROTT'S HEMKE: GOLD AND SILVER 2026 LOWS ARE LIKELY IN — FUNDAMENTALS INTACT AS WEST SELLS INTO PBOC'S STEADY BID
snippet: Craig Hemke of Sprott Money told Kitco News on July 7 that gold and silver have most likely set their 2026 price lows and should resume their structural bull move once the current technically-bearish configuration resolves — with prices below all key moving averages but supported by a historically wide divergence between Western institutional selling and the PBOC's ongoing price-insensitive accumulation. Hemke's thesis rests on the observation that current price weakness is a rate-repricing and geopolitical reaction, not a demand event: physical offtake from India, China, and central banks has not declined even as futures markets have driven prices lower, and a return to fundamental pricing once technical selling exhausts should unlock the next leg of the structural bull that the WGC's mid-year outlook also identified as intact.

headline: INZINC COMPLETES B-9 APEX FOLLOW-UP — 1,000M STRIKE ON 20.1% ZN SEDEX FIND PLUS GALLIUM BYPRODUCT, ASSAYS DUE (TSXV:IZN)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / InZinc Mining Ltd.
snippet: InZinc Mining (TSXV: IZN) announced July 9 the completion of a 7-hole, 1,437-metre spring 2026 diamond drill program at the Indy Sedex project in central BC — following up on the 2025 B-9 Apex discovery (15.4% Zn, 1.3% Pb, 7.2 g/t Ag over 4.2m; inner 20.1% Zn over 3.2m) after extending the B-9 trend to over 1,000 metres in strike length, with the new program testing 250 metres of strike north and south of the discovery hole to 240 metres depth. The Indy project hosts zinc-lead-silver mineralisation alongside gallium — a critical semiconductor and 5G metal in short supply outside China — in a near-surface Sedex setting 90 kilometres southeast of Prince George; assays from all seven holes are pending and represent one of the more anticipated zinc-gallium discovery datasets currently in the Canadian junior exploration pipeline.
